newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet sued by Nashville airport - paper.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet sued by Nashville airport - paper.

text.p: ValuJet Inc faced a $2.5 million lawsuit for terminating its airport lease in Nashville, Tenn., the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported on Wednesday.

The Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority filed the suit to reclaim the value of a lease that was to run until 2017. ValuJet terminated the lease in July, citing a provision allowing it to do so if prevented from using the facility by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration, the newspaper said.
Airline officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.
ValuJet has been grounded since mid-June because of safety problems found by FAA inspectors in the wake of its May 11 crash in the Florida Everglades, which killed 110 people.
The Journal-Constitution said the Nashville lease was one of several airport leases to have been pulled by ValuJet in a bid to save cash during its grounding.
